Alyssa: quick heads up — saw a perf regression in latest canary when fused_flash_v2 + interleaved KV are used with bfloat16 workloads. p50 tokens/sec down ~18% on chat_long traces.
Mateo: ouch. same model/config as last stable run?
Alyssa: yes, same model (redwood-7B-compat), same seq dist. only change was kernel selector preferring fused_flash_v2 for seq_len>1024.
Priya: any obvious hotspot from nvprof/triton logs?
Alyssa: profiler snapshot:
```
== Kernel timeline (sample) ==
fused_flash_v2_forward  |  12.4ms  |  mem_wait 2.3ms  |  warp_stall 3.1ms
kv_page_copy           |   6.8ms  |  unaligned_loads 4.9ms
flash_attention_fallback|  18.9ms
```
Alyssa: mem_wait spikes on the kv_page_copy path when layout=interleaved and dtype=bf16. memcpy-ish patterns look like many small unaligned loads.
Dan: that smells like alignment + stride mismatch between page-aligned buffers and interleaved layout. did the kernel assume 128-bit alignment?
Alyssa: yes, fused_flash_v2 assumes 16-byte alignment for vector loads. interleaved KV gives per-key offsets that are not always 16-byte aligned for bf16 packing -> generates extra instructions on load.
Mateo: numbers?
Alyssa: microbench (single GPU, p3-type):
```
config A: fused_flash_v2 + interleaved + bf16 -> 82k tokens/s (p50)
config B: fused_flash_v2 + separate_kv + bf16 -> 101k tokens/s (p50)
config C: flash_fallback + interleaved + bf16 -> 95k tokens/s (p50)
```
Alyssa: so fused_flash_v2 + interleaved is worst. fallback kernel avoids those unaligned vector ops.
Priya: is this strictly an interleaved packing issue? what about dtype=float16?
Alyssa: float16 lanes naturally align differently. float16 + interleaved doesn't show the same degradation (only ~3% diff). bf16 packing moves bytes around for packing 2 bytes -> 4 byte alignment assumptions break.
Dan: might be a quick mitigation to adjust the kernel selector: prefer separate_kv for bf16 until we fix vector load path. Also we can add an alignment check and force pad to 16B when allocating interleaved pages.
Mateo: padding pages will increase memory slightly but could avoid perf cliff. what about continuous batching behavior? could that amplify the issue?
Alyssa: yes — larger batches increase chance of misaligned per-request offsets, so the mem stalls scale with batch size. I saw the regression more pronounced with batch_size>=8.
Priya: other signal from tracer? any increased L2 miss rate?
Alyssa: L2 misses up ~2x for the bad config, and serialized scalar loads show up in SASS.
Dan: plan: 1) short term selector change (separate_kv for bf16 OR disable fused_flash_v2 for interleaved). 2) add allocator pad-to-16B option behind a flag. 3) longer term, update fused_flash_v2 to handle unaligned bf16 loads (vectorize differently).
Mateo: can you push a canary with selector change? i'll run nightly perf suite.
Alyssa: on it — pushing a patch to canary branch now. ci-bot: build started (canary/fused-kernel-selector-patch).
ci-bot: build succeeded. canary image pushed -> gcr.redwood/canary:fused-kv-bf16-fix
Priya: i'll run evals on SLO-critical routes tomorrow morning and report regressions.
Alyssa: thanks — tagging this thread for follow-up after nightly runs. if we confirm, we'll roll selector tweak to stable and open a runtime issue to track kernel work. :thumbsup:
Mateo: 👍
Dan: +1
Alyssa: quick note for the changelog: selector heuristic now checks: if (dtype==bf16 && layout==interleaved && batch_size>=4) -> prefer separate_kv or flash_fallback.
Priya: please add a flag to opt into pad-to-16B: `REDWOOD_KV_PAD_BYTES=16` for testing.
Alyssa: added to canary env and docs.
Mateo: nice. we'll keep an eye on unit cost impact if padding increases memory pressure.
Alyssa: yep — will run mem/regression sweep too.
